title: BreakPoint AI: Momentum Modeling in ATP Tennis
text:
Executive Summary
Sports betting markets are notoriously efficient; a static model relying on average statistics will rarely beat the “closing line.” This project treats a tennis match not as a row of data, but as the collision of two historical trajectories.
By implementing a Hybrid Siamese LSTM, I moved beyond static feature engineering to capture latent “momentum,” achieving institutional-grade performance:

Market Edge: Achieved 0.706 AUC, reaching statistical parity with institutional bookmakers in a high-variance domain.
Risk Calibration: Delivered a perfectly calibrated probability engine (Expected Value \(\approx\) Actual Value), essential for Kelly Criterion staking.
Innovation: Developed a “Twin Network” architecture that learns player form independently before assessing the specific matchup.




1. The Market Problem

The “Static Stats” Fallacy
Standard sports modeling suffers from a critical flaw: it aggregates performance (e.g., “Player A serves 65% first in”) into a single static number. This ignores Momentum—the temporal reality that a player’s form fluctuates significantly over a season.


The Objective
Build a system that answers: “Given the exact sequence of the last 10 matches for Player A and Player B, what is the probability of Player A winning today?”
Crucially, this system must avoid Look-Ahead Bias, ensuring that no future information leaks into the training set—a common pitfall in academic sports papers.




2. System Architecture
To capture this temporal dynamic, I utilized a Siamese (Twin) Architecture. The network processes each player’s history independently to generate a “Momentum Embedding” before fusion.

Model Diagram






graph TD
    subgraph SP ["Sequence Processing (Twin LSTMs)"]
        A["Player A History<br/>(Last 10 Matches)"] -->|LSTM| E1[Momentum Embedding A]
        B["Player B History<br/>(Last 10 Matches)"] -->|LSTM| E2[Momentum Embedding B]
    end

    subgraph CF ["Context Fusion"]
        C["Static Context<br/>(Rank, Surface, H2H)"] --> F[Fusion Layer]
        E1 --> F
        E2 --> F
    end

    F -->|Dense + Dropout| O[Win Probability]

    style F fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style O fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px





Figure 1: Hybrid Siamese LSTM Architecture









3. Modeling Strategy

Benchmarking Complexity
I compared the deep learning approach against an industry-standard baseline to justify the computational cost.

Random Forest (Baseline): Trained on manually engineered rolling averages (e.g., “Avg Aces Last 5 Matches”).
Siamese LSTM (Challenger): Trained on raw, sequential match logs.

Winner: Tie (with a caveat). The LSTM matched the Random Forest in accuracy (~64.6%) without needing manual feature engineering. This validates that the neural network successfully “learned” the rolling statistics and momentum features automatically from the raw sequence.




4. Results & Analysis

Performance Metrics
The final model demonstrated robust separation power between winners and losers.









Metric
Random Forest (Baseline)
Siamese LSTM (Ours)
Insight




Test AUC
0.7062
0.7060
Parity achieved with engineered baseline.


Accuracy
64.67%
64.61%
Consistent edge over coin-flip noise.





Business Insight: The Calibration Curve
In quantitative finance, accuracy is secondary to Calibration. If a model says “70% confidence,” the event must happen 70% of the time to be profitable.
The plot below shows the LSTM’s reliability. The Orange line (Model) closely hugs the Blue line (Perfect Calibration).



Calibration Curve for LSTM Model








Betting Implication: The model knows what it doesn’t know. Because the probabilities are honest (calibrated), this model can be directly plugged into a Kelly Criterion sizing strategy to maximize long-term bankroll growth without the risk of ruin caused by overconfidence.







5. Key Drivers (Interpretation)
While the LSTM acts as the “Engine,” we use the Random Forest baseline to explain the “Why” (Proxy Analysis).



SHAP Value for Random Forests


SHAP Value Analysis:

Rank Difference (rank_diff): The market anchor. The widening gap in ranking remains the single strongest predictor.
Momentum (win_pct_roll_diff): The difference in recent win percentage is the critical secondary factor.
Serve Metrics (svpt): Performance on serve points acts as a granular proxy for player dominance.




Conclusion
This project demonstrates the application of Deep Learning to Time-Series Forecasting in a hostile, high-noise environment.
By strictly enforcing time-series validation and prioritizing probability calibration over raw accuracy, BreakPoint AI bridges the gap between “sports data science” and quantitative financial modeling.

text: This project analyzes 4.5 million Uber pickups in New York City to identify high-demand locations and time windows. How does fleet activity shift between weekdays and weekends?

title: Uber NYC Demand Analysis (Apr–Sep 2014)
text:
1. Geographic Distribution
Question: Is demand spread evenly across the city?

Finding: The pickup density is heavily skewed.

Manhattan Core: The vast majority of rides occur in Manhattan (below 59th St) and Downtown Brooklyn.
Airport Clusters: Outside the city grid, the only significant hotspots are JFK and LaGuardia Airports.
Operational Insight: For a driver, leaving Manhattan without an airport fare is statistically inefficient, as return trips from outer boroughs are rare.

title: Uber NYC Demand Analysis (Apr–Sep 2014)
text:
2. Hourly Demand Patterns
Question: Is there a consistent “best time” to drive?

Finding:Demand follows a strict daily cycle that is consistent across all six months (Apr–Sep).

The Build-Up: Ride volume begins to rise significantly at 16:00 (4 PM).
The Peak: The busiest hour is consistently 17:00–18:00 (5–6 PM), coinciding with the end of the traditional workday.
Late Night: Demand tapers off after 21:00, except on weekends (see below).

title: Uber NYC Demand Analysis (Apr–Sep 2014)
text:
3. Heatmap Analysis: Day vs. Hour
Question: How does the schedule change from Tuesday to Saturday?

Finding: Aggregating data by day of the week reveals two distinct distinct “shifts”:

The Commuter Shift (Mon–Thu): Demand is strictly focused on rush hours (07:00–09:00 and 17:00–19:00).
The Nightlife Shift (Fri–Sat): The evening peak extends well past midnight, staying high until 02:00 AM.

Business Implication: Algorithms should prioritize “commuter” routes during the week but switch to “entertainment district” positioning on Friday nights.

title: Uber NYC Demand Analysis (Apr–Sep 2014)
text:
4. Base Growth (Fleet Scaling)
Question: Are all Uber bases growing at the same rate?

Finding: While most bases (like B02598 and B02682) showed stable monthly volume, Base B02617 (Teal) grew exponentially.

April: ~30k trips
September: ~180k trips
This suggests that Uber likely consolidated drivers into this specific base or ran an aggressive onboarding campaign during the summer of 2014.

title: Optimizing Credit Risk: A Profit-First Approach
text:
Executive Summary
In consumer lending, accuracy is a misleading metric. A model that blindly predicts “No Default” can achieve 85% accuracy but bankrupt a lender by missing the few massive defaults.
This project re-engineers the credit scoring process by shifting the optimization objective from Statistical Accuracy (F1-Score) to Economic Profit.
By developing a modular classification engine and applying a custom profit-maximization threshold, this strategy achieved:

Financial Impact: Projected portfolio value of $1.26M, a ~40% ROI lift over the baseline.
Risk Policy: Identified an optimal cutoff rejecting the riskiest 17.3% of applicants.
Model Performance: Achieved a 0.685 ROC-AUC using a defensible, regulator-friendly Logistic Regression model.




1. The Business Problem

Asymmetry of Errors
In credit risk, confusion matrix errors are not created equal:

False Positive (Type I Error): We reject a good applicant. Cost = Opportunity Cost of Interest.
False Negative (Type II Error): We approve a defaulter. Cost = Loss of Principal.

Since the Principal is significantly larger than the Interest, avoiding False Negatives is mathematically more critical than avoiding False Positives. Standard “out-of-the-box” machine learning models often fail to capture this asymmetry by themselves.


The Objective
Build a system that answers: “What is the exact probability threshold that maximizes Net Portfolio Profit?”




2. System Architecture
To ensure reproducibility and prevent data leakage, I moved beyond ad-hoc notebooks to a production-grade modular architecture.

Directory Structure
The project is organized as a Python package (src), separating business logic from training pipelines.
├── src/
│   ├── data_pipeline.py  # Custom Transformers (Financial Engineering)
│   ├── training.py       # Cross-Validation & Hyperparameter Tuning
│   ├── evaluation.py     # Profit & Strategy Curve Logic
│   └── config.py         # Centralized Assumptions
├── notebooks/            # Narrative Analysis
└── README.md


Feature Engineering Pipeline
A critical component was the FinancialFeatureEngineer transformer, which derives economic variables before the model sees the data. This calculates the Present Value (PV) of the loan using standard amortization formulas.
# src/data_pipeline.py Snippet

def engineer_financial_features(df):
    """
    Derives the Principal (PV) using the Annuity Formula.
    PV = Installment * (1 - (1+r)^-n) / r
    """
    monthly_rate = df['int.rate'] / 12
    term = 36 # Assumed 36-month term
    
    # Vectorized Calculation of Risk Exposure
    df['principal'] = df['installment'] * (
        1 - (1 + monthly_rate)**(-term)
    ) / monthly_rate
    
    return df




3. Modeling Strategy

Model Selection
I benchmarked three architectures:

Logistic Regression: Linear, highly interpretable (industry standard for compliance).
Random Forest: Handles non-linearities but prone to overfitting on noise.
XGBoost: Gradient boosting for maximizing weak signals.

Winner: Logistic Regression. Surprisingly, the simpler linear model outperformed the complex tree ensembles on the test set (AUC 0.685 vs 0.67 & 0.66 respectively). This suggests the signal in this specific dataset is largely linear (e.g., FICO scores linearly correlate with risk), and the complex models were overfitting the noise.


The “Strategy Curve”
Instead of accepting the default decision threshold of 0.5, I implemented a custom evaluation function to plot Profit vs. Approval Rate.

X-Axis: Percentage of loans approved (sorted by safety).
Y-Axis: Total Portfolio Profit.

 This visualization allows stakeholders to visually “pick” their risk appetite.




4. Results & Analysis

Performance Metrics
The final model demonstrated robust separation power between “Good” and “Bad” loans.

ROC-AUC: 0.685
Precision (Class 0 - Paid): 0.86
Recall (Class 1 - Default): Tunable via threshold.



Business Insight: The Optimization Peak
The analysis revealed a convex profit curve.

At 100% Approval: The portfolio absorbs all toxic assets, significantly reducing net profit.
At 82.7% Approval (The Peak): By cutting the bottom 17.3% of risky applicants, we maximize profit at $1,264,043.
Below 80% Approval: We start rejecting too many good customers, and the opportunity cost (lost interest) begins to outweigh the savings from avoided defaults.







Managerial Conclusion: The optimal policy is strict but not draconian. We should approve the safest ~83% of applicants. This creates a projected 40% increase in profitability compared to a naive strategy.







5. Key Risk Drivers (Interpretation)
Using coefficient analysis (and SHAP values for tree benchmarks), the primary drivers of default were:

FICO Score: The single strongest predictor. Lower scores exponentially increase default odds.
Inquiries (Last 6 Months): A high velocity of recent credit applications is a strong distress signal.
Interest Rate: The market is efficient—loans priced with higher rates did default more often, confirming that the original underwriters correctly identified risk (though they often underpriced it).




Conclusion
This project demonstrates that Data Science is not just about prediction; it is about decision-making.
By translating a classification problem into a financial optimization problem, I delivered a model that speaks the language of the business: Profit, ROI, and Risk Exposure.

title: About Me
text:
Finding Truth in the NoiseEncontrando Verdade no Ruído
My name is Rafael Condé Gomes, and I am a senior at the University of South Florida, pursuing a dual degree in Econometrics & Quantitative Economics and Information Science (Data Science & Analytics). My journey to this field did not begin in a computer lab, but on a tennis court in Brazil. As the #1 ranked junior player in Rio de Janeiro and a top-20 national athlete, I spent years obsessing over performance. In sports, you can lie to yourself about how good you are, but the scoreboard never lies. That early exposure to brutal, objective reality shaped my entire worldview: I trust results, not narratives.Meu nome é Rafael Condé Gomes, e sou estudante de último ano na University of South Florida, cursando dupla graduação em Econometria & Economia Quantitativa e Ciência da Informação (Data Science & Analytics). Minha trajetória até essa área não começou em um laboratório, mas em uma quadra de tênis no Brasil. Como tenista #1 no ranking júnior do Rio de Janeiro e atleta top-20 nacional, passei anos obcecado com desempenho. No esporte, você pode se enganar sobre o quanto é bom — mas o placar nunca mente. Essa exposição precoce a uma realidade brutal e objetiva moldou minha visão de mundo: confio em resultados, não em narrativas.


The Crisis of Validity: What the Field Needs NowA Crise de Validade: O Que o Campo Precisa Agora
The financial and economic sectors are currently facing a crisis of validity. The industry is saturated with methodologies that persist solely due to institutional inertia rather than empirical success. We see this in the dominance of active management, which repeatedly fails to outperform passive benchmarks, and in the reliance on valuation models like Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) or trading multiples. These tools are mathematically elegant, but they often rely on fragile assumptions that crumble under real-world variance.Os setores financeiro e econômico enfrentam uma crise de validade. A indústria está saturada de metodologias que persistem apenas por inércia institucional, não por sucesso empírico. Vemos isso na dominância da gestão ativa — que repetidamente falha em superar benchmarks passivos — e na dependência de modelos como Fluxo de Caixa Descontado (DCF) ou múltiplos de trading. Essas ferramentas são matematicamente elegantes, mas frequentemente dependem de premissas frágeis que se desfazem diante da variância do mundo real.
The critical weakness in the field today is a lack of rigorous performance measurement. Models are often deployed because they are “industry standard,” not because they have been stress-tested against the chaotic reality of actual markets. The industry does not need more analysts who can recite textbook formulas; it needs scientists who can falsify them. My interest in Data Science is driven by this specific gap. I believe the future of finance belongs to those who view markets not through the lens of dogma or “gut feeling,” but through the rigorous application of the scientific method. We must replace “this is how we’ve always done it” with “this is what the evidence proves.”A fraqueza crítica do campo hoje é a falta de mensuração rigorosa de desempenho. Modelos são implementados porque são “padrão do setor”, não porque foram testados contra a realidade caótica dos mercados. A indústria não precisa de mais analistas que recitam fórmulas de livros; precisa de cientistas que possam falsificá-las. Meu interesse em Data Science é motivado exatamente por essa lacuna. Acredito que o futuro das finanças pertence a quem enxerga os mercados não pelo prisma do dogma ou do “instinto”, mas pela aplicação rigorosa do método científico. Precisamos substituir “é assim que sempre fizemos” por “é isso que a evidência prova.”


The Storyteller: Translating Complexity into ActionO Tradutor: Transformando Complexidade em Ação
However, generating evidence is only half the battle. Data is cold, and without context, it is useless to decision-makers. A complex neural network is a black box if a CEO or a client cannot understand its implications for their bottom line. This is where my “soft skills” come into play. I view the Data Scientist not just as a coder, but as a translator.No entanto, gerar evidências é apenas metade do trabalho. Dados são frios e, sem contexto, inúteis para quem toma decisões. Uma rede neural complexa é uma caixa preta se um CEO ou cliente não consegue entender suas implicações para o resultado financeiro. É aqui que minhas habilidades de comunicação entram. Vejo o Cientista de Dados não apenas como programador, mas como tradutor.
In my role as Technology Director at Hexa Consulting, I learned that my most valuable skill wasn’t my ability to write Python scripts, but my ability to craft a narrative around the output. I focus on “Data Storytelling”: the art of structuring technical findings into a clear argument that drives action. If I tell a stakeholder that “the model has a 0.78 F1-score,” it means nothing. But if I tell them, “This model identifies the specific inefficiencies that are costing us 15% in wasted capital,” I have solved a problem. My goal is to present complex evidence so clearly that the correct decision becomes obvious to everyone in the room.No meu papel como Diretor de Tecnologia na Hexa Consulting, aprendi que minha habilidade mais valiosa não era escrever scripts Python, mas construir uma narrativa em torno dos resultados. Foco em “Data Storytelling”: a arte de estruturar descobertas técnicas em um argumento claro que gera ação. Se digo a um stakeholder que “o modelo tem F1-score de 0,78”, não significa nada. Mas se digo “Este modelo identifica as ineficiências específicas que nos custam 15% em capital desperdiçado”, resolvi um problema. Meu objetivo é apresentar evidências complexas com tanta clareza que a decisão correta se torna óbvia para todos na sala.


Technical Competence & Academic RigorCompetência Técnica & Rigor Acadêmico
My ability to critique current methods is backed by a robust technical foundation. My concentration in Data Science & Analytics has equipped me with a strong stack in Python (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn, PyTorch) and R for statistical analysis. I don’t just run existing software; I build systems to test my hypotheses.Minha capacidade de criticar métodos atuais é respaldada por uma base técnica sólida. Minha concentração em Data Science & Analytics me equipou com um stack robusto em Python (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn, PyTorch) e R para análise estatística. Não apenas executo softwares existentes; construo sistemas para testar minhas hipóteses.
For instance, in my Credit Risk Optimization project, I didn’t just maximize accuracy; I built a custom engine to maximize profit, proving that I understand the economic reality behind the code. Similarly, my BreakPoint AI project used Hybrid Siamese LSTMs to forecast tennis matches. While standard betting markets rely on static stats, I modeled “momentum” as a time-series problem, achieving parity with institutional bookmakers. These projects are not just academic exercises; they are proof that a data-centric approach can outperform human intuition.Por exemplo, no meu projeto de Credit Risk Optimization, não apenas maximizei acurácia; construí um motor personalizado para maximizar lucro, provando que entendo a realidade econômica por trás do código. Da mesma forma, meu projeto BreakPoint AI usou Hybrid Siamese LSTMs para prever partidas de tênis. Enquanto mercados de apostas dependem de estatísticas estáticas, modelei “momentum” como um problema de séries temporais, alcançando paridade com casas de apostas institucionais. Esses projetos não são apenas exercícios acadêmicos; são prova de que uma abordagem centrada em dados pode superar a intuição humana.


Career Goals & Future OutlookObjetivos de Carreira & Perspectivas
As I approach graduation in May 2026, my objective is to secure a role as a Data Scientist or Quantitative Analyst. I am specifically targeting high-performance environments—such as hedge funds, proprietary trading firms, or tech-forward financial institutions—where accuracy and inference are paramount. I am driven by a hunger to build things that actually work in production.Com a formatura em maio de 2026, meu objetivo é conquistar uma posição como Cientista de Dados ou Analista Quantitativo. Estou mirando especificamente em ambientes de alta performance — como hedge funds, proprietary trading firms ou instituições financeiras orientadas a tecnologia — onde precisão e inferência são fundamentais.
